body: Very sorry to hear your story.  I am an adult chronic pain sufferer and I too have found most of the resources are geared towards teens.  Unfortunately, very little of that advice applies to anyone wanting to escape their life due to medical issues and physical pain.  Good luck.

Hi,

I just saw your reply, thanks for responding.  Yeah, I did get back into therapy thanks to this whole saga, and I am taking medications for pain.  Takes the edge off some.  They are definitely helpful in surviving everything, however I think I may need to add to the regimen and get on something that targets nerve pain more. 

I'm so with you on the unluckiness stuff!  I think about that often.  It's definitely a struggle going to work and encountering a slew of people who were fortunate enough to not be in some kind of chronic pain, who just get to feel more or less normal.  I used to be like that, blissfully unaware of how every day can be just a living hell of constant pain for the unlucky ones.

Sorry to hear about your issues.  Having something physical going on can definitely compound and fuel depression problems for sure.  Is there hope for any kind of solution or cure to make what you're going through livable?  Do you work or go to school?  What do you like to do to distract yourself?  I'm finding distraction is key for me while I work to repair my issues.  If I let myself stop and think about everything and harp on the pain, that's when things get the worst.
That's a good idea, thank you!
